content: {"summary":"Orders‑api, auth‑service and catalog‑api saw lookup timeouts caused by an overloaded CoreDNS deployment; scaling the CoreDNS pods cleared the failures.","likely_cause":"CoreDNS pods were saturated (high CPU and latency), causing DNS resolution timeouts for prod.internal names.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The affected services were reported healthy at the time of the incident","evidence_ids":["status:orders-api","status:auth-service","status:catalog-api"],"quote":"orders-api: healthy (owner team-commerce; depends on orders-db, payments-api, inventory-service, kafka)"},{"text":"Name resolution began failing for catalog‑api, orders‑api and auth‑service at 19:50","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"19:50 catalog-api, orders-api, auth-service: name resolution begins failing, all at once"},{"text":"CoreDNS pods were at their CPU ceiling and request latency spiked to seconds","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"20:05 CoreDNS dashboard: request p99 is measured in seconds now, while the query volume is only at the upper end of a normal evening"},{"text":"Scaling CoreDNS to four replicas restored DNS lookups","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"20:08 scaled coredns to 4 replicas"}],"next_checks":["Monitor CoreDNS CPU usage and request latency continuously","Set up alerts for DNS query failures (EAI_AGAIN, no such host)","Verify rollout tool updates of prod.internal zone are atomic or use dual‑write safety","Consider autoscaling CoreDNS based on query load"]}
